sentences.text: This dinosaur measured roughly four meters in length and weighed about 250 kilograms, although some individuals may have grown to six meters long.
Other estimates suggest a running animal standing 1.7 meters high with a total length of 4.5 meters and a mass of 500 kilograms.
It moved by alternating between walking on two legs and walking on four legs.
Its front limbs possessed four fingers used for handling food, while its hind feet ended in hoof-like nails designed for quick escapes.
The name of the genus translates to "grooved tooth," and the specific name means "primitive."
This creature appeared in the Discovery Channel series Dinosaur Planet, where it was called the "dwarf Iguanodon."
Fossil remains have been uncovered in southern France and in fragmentary form in eastern Spain.
Today, known remains also extend to Romania.
Similar limb and femur fragments have been found in the Czech Republic.
The type species was first named by Matheron in 1869, though it was originally given two different spellings.
In 1986, Winand Brinkmann asked the ICZN to suppress an earlier use of the name by Fleischmann from 1831 and to officially set the specific name as priscus.
Eric Buffetaut and Jean Le Loueff later named a second species, Rhabdodon septimanicus, in 1991.
Philippe Matheron formally named Rhabdodon priscus in 1869.
A second species, R. septimanicus, was described in 1991 by Buffetaut and Le Loeuff.
It was likely an herbivore living in Cretaceous Europe.
Isotope analysis shows that this animal ate C3 plants.
A hard beak and multiple rows of teeth allowed it to crush tougher foods.
A 2012 study by Ősi et al. suggested that Rhabdodon experienced gigantism on the mainland rather than insular dwarfism.
However, Rhabdodon priscus was of small size because it lived in an insular environment like Europe was at that time.
The material of R. priscus includes a lower jaw bone and many other bones from the rest of the body.
Rhabdodon belongs to the family Rhabdodontidae.
The parent group of Rhabdodon is Rhabdodontidae.
It is classified in the class Ornithischia.
Modern phylogenetic analyses classify Rhabdodon as a basal member of Iguanodontia rather than a hypsilophodont.
Rhabdodon is structurally similar to a robust hypsilophodontid but is classified by modern phylogenetic analyses as a basal member of Iguanodontia.
The name has had synonyms including Rabdodon, Oligosaurus, and Ornithomerus.
Rhabdodon lived in Europe during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 72 to 66 million years ago.
It lived during the Late Cretaceous (Maastrichtian), approximately 70 to 66 million years ago, in what is now Europe.
Rhabdodon lived during the Campanian to Maastrichtian stages, from 83.6 to 66 million years ago.
The Lo Hueco region where fossils were found was near the coast of the Tethys Sea.
The environment near the Lo Hueco fossil site included a brackish-freshwater aquatic area and a muddy floodplain.
Rhabdodon priscus is known from specimens found in the Marnes Rouges Inférieures Formation.
It is also known from the Gres de Saint-Chinian Formation.
It is debated whether the second species R. septimanicus, described from an isolated jaw fragment, is distinct or belongs to the same species as R. priscus.
A 2026 study by Maidment et al. suggested some specimens previously classified as rhabdodontids might actually belong to Ceratopsoidea.
